output.evidence: Version 4 (image 8) fulfills the terracotta arch-wall concept most completely: the shallow arched niche is fully formed and symmetrically centered behind the bottle so the packshot sits at the arch heart, slightly right of frame, while the left text column (brand, headline, EAU DE PARFUM, thin rule) keeps the asymmetric two-column grid intact. Typography is coherent and legible in the warm earth palette; the暗 glass keeps crisp frontal highlights against the sun-baked plaster. Crucially, the niche floor reads as a real resting plane: the bottle base meets it with a soft contact shadow, giving convincing physical contact, and proportions stay inside the safety bounds (top ~25%, base ~91%, height ~66%). Version 1 hides the niche almost entirely behind the bottle and leaves it floating; version 2 shifts the niche off to the left so the bottle overlaps its jamb; version 3 places the niche sill behind the bottle at mid-height, breaking the standing logic; version 5 fractures the type column (rule detached above EAU DE PARFUM) and.darkens the niche into a muddy hole with weaker text contrast.
remaining_problems: Version 4's contact shadow under the base is faint; the bottle still reads slightly pasted onto the niche floor rather than weighted into it.
The niche interior in version 4 is quite dark at the crown, muting the promised warm ambient bounce inside the arch.
Left column rule sits close to the headline block, leaving the lower left field emptier than the concept's balanced two-column grid intends.
Plaster texture shows mild painterly smearing around the arch edge rather than crisp sun-baked grain.
